plan.title: UC inflamed vs control hallmark GSVA sample scores
plan.analytical_narrative: The research question asks for a per-sample pathway activity score and a hallmark heatmap that shows which pathways separate ulcerative colitis inflamed colon from control. The inputs are a 12000 x 13 CSV of raw Salmon gene-level counts keyed by gene symbol and a 12 x 2 sample table with one condition column: 6 UC-inflamed vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch. Because the question is a score per sample across many gene sets, tested as one matrix under a fixed design, GSVA is the right single-sample method (the knowledge service lists it as the permitted alternative to UCell exactly for this case: many sets, fixed sample set, limma on the score matrix). The caveat that sample_01 has a library size about 4x below the median drives step T1S1: the sample is kept, inspected on the PCA and distance heatmap, and its depth reported, not silently dropped — median-of-ratios size factors already account for depth, and a GSVA score is computed on a variance-stabilized matrix where the within-sample ranking is depth-robust. T1S2 applies the minimal pre-filter (>=10 counts in >=6 samples, the smallest group size) and produces the VST matrix that scoring consumes. T2S1 scores the 50 MSigDB human hallmark sets per sample, tests each score with limma under ~condition with control as the explicit reference level, and adjusts across the 50 sets with Benjamini-Hochberg. T2S2 draws the deliverable heatmap of hallmark scores across the 12 samples, annotated by condition and by library size so a reader can see whether the low-depth sample drives any block, and writes the reproducibility record. No differential expression at gene level is planned — the question does not ask for it, and the score-level test is the inference here. With 6 vs 6 the score-level test has 12 units, not 12000, so a hallmark that fails BH is not evidence of no difference; the steps must say so.

Hallmark activity heatmap across samples with reproducibility record
